official_sources: GOV.UK flexible options for planning permissions

official_measurement_examples.fact: There is no statutory definition of non-material; the local planning authority must assess materiality in the context of the existing permission.
Section 96A cannot be used for a material amendment.
A successful s96A decision does not create a new planning permission; the original permission and amendment decision must be read together.
The s96A procedure applies to planning permissions and cannot be used to amend listed building consent.
The authority must consider the effect of the proposed change together with previous s96A changes.
A s96A refusal does not carry the normal section 78 appeal route; a different application route may be required.
Current local-authority guidance in 2026 continues to distinguish s96A from section 73 and fresh planning applications.
s96A approval does not establish ownership, statutory-consent compliance, infrastructure capacity or development yield.

core_rules: non-material has no universal numeric threshold
s96A does not create a new planning permission
s96A cannot amend listed building consent
s96A refusal has distinct appeal position
approval does not prove condition compliance
approval does not establish infrastructure capacity
decision date and original permission must be retained
no parcel amendment clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
